Real NASA data (after play): the site is Connecting Ridge (an Artemis III candidate region) from LRO LOLA laser altimetry (40 m and 240 m polar DEMs), with lunar curvature; the Sun and Earth follow JPL Horizons positions for each mission's real 2027 date; permanently shadowed cells come from a whole year of real Sun positions. Baked into one offline file. After play: the heights are blended halfway toward a 0.5 km smoothed copy so the rover can drive it (terrain_smooth, 0 = raw data), and the credits say so; the stations sit within about 3.5 km of a ridge-top start zone, with a real shadowed hollow for the cold-trap drill.

KPI score and site debrief (after play): each mission is graded A-F on six KPIs (science sent, crew home, lander sunlit %, dish Earth %, lowest battery, science left unsent) against targets, with points, a big mission score, the campaign total and a rating; the debrief compares your landing site's Sun/Earth timeline with the planner's pick among about 1000 landable sites and says why it is better.

Numbered walkthrough (after play): on the first mission, 7 steps in orbit and 6 after touchdown light one part of the screen at a time and explain the controls, what the live numbers mean and what makes a good landing site; H shows it again.

Planner Mode and Validation (after play, for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge): P on the title opens a planner on any hour of 2027 (hour, day and week steps, window 24 h to 708 h, time-lapse), named published sites, typed latitude/longitude limited to the baked map, up to 3 sites compared with Sun %, Earth %, Sun clearance and next sunset/Earthset, a slip test (+1 d, +3 d, +7 d) and a best-sites heat map; V opens a validation screen that recomputes sunlight at 4 published sites (Gläser et al. 2017), Sun and Earth elevations against independent JPL Horizons topocentric queries, and the Shackleton floor shadow check, with method and limits.
